info.title: Qlix Developer API
info.description:
Account-scoped programmatic access to Qlix Layer 3 (agent identity), Layer 5 (audit ledger), agent/team executions, AI Brain, and AI Builder (natural-language parse/create plus visual canvases).

## Authentication
Create keys in the console under **API**. Send `Authorization: Bearer qlix_live_…` (recommended) or `X-Api-Key: qlix_live_…`. Keys are hashed at rest; the secret is shown once.

API keys are scoped. Session JWT (the console cookie) is not restricted by these scopes. A key acts as the **creating user** (same org and role) — for example `GET /compliance/export` still requires owner/admin even with `audit:read`. The key is stored with that organization at creation; writes (create agent, NL create, teams, brain) use it automatically. Do not send `orgId` in request bodies.

Four auth modes exist in Qlix. Only the first is this API:
1. **API key** (`qlix_live_*`) — this Developer API.
2. **Session JWT** — console browser cookie; also accepted as Bearer, but not for key management from scripts.
3. **Agent-signed** Ed25519 payloads — `POST /actions/*` and `POST /jit/request` (Python agent SDK).
4. **Runner token** (`X-QLIX-Runner-Token`) — cloud/hybrid agent runtime, not account scripts.

Key CRUD (`/api-keys`) is session-only (`403 session_required` if you use an API key).

## Rate limits
- API keys: **300 requests/minute** per key (override `API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`).
- Other clients: **600 requests/minute** per IP (`GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`).
- `429` body: `{ "error": { "code": "rate_limited", "message": "…" } }`.

## Subscription
Mutating routes (create agent, NL create, enqueue runs, team runs, brain writes, canvas writes) require an active workspace subscription, same as the console.

## Errors
All errors use `{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string } }`. Common codes: `unauthorized`, `insufficient_scope`, `api_key_not_allowed`, `session_required`, `rate_limited`, `invalid_body`, `not_found`.

## Documented vs allowlisted
This spec covers first-class Developer API operations. Some additional mutations under `/teams/{id}/*` (`teams:write`) and `/ai-brain/*` (`brain:write`) are allowlisted but not listed individually.

tags.description: Just-in-time human approvals. The request is delivered to the channel that started the run; that same source sends approve/deny (API: POST /jit/decide, console card, WhatsApp yes/no). Pending requests expire if unanswered; some scopes become a conversation grant after one yes.

ApiKeyBearer.description: API key issued from the Qlix console

orgId.description: Optional. API keys ignore this field and always use the org bound to the key at creation. Session (console) callers may omit it to use the signed-in org, or pass null for individual-workspace agent rows.

sourceChannel.description: Where the run started: api, web, whatsapp, slack, telegram, local, cron

orgId.description: Optional. API keys ignore this field and always use the org bound to the key. Session callers may omit it to use the signed-in org.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked API key / session

Forbidden.description: Missing scope, role, or route not in the Developer API

get.summary: Read the user and organization bound to this API key
get.description: Returns the user and organization already bound to this API key (`user.orgId` and `organization.id` are the same UUID). Create and other writes infer the workspace from the key — you do not pass `orgId` in request bodies.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Optional. Omit to use the workspace bound to the API key. Session callers may pass this to filter; it must match the signed-in org.

post.description: Decide a pending JIT request created by a running agent. Use this when the run was started with this API key (or from the console). WhatsApp/Slack-originated runs are decided in those chats instead.

get.description: Lists pending JIT approvals for the key's user. Omit filters to see every waiting request. Pass `runId` to scope to one run, or `conversationId`+`agentId` for a chat thread. Approvals for API-started runs appear here and as `jit_approval_pending` on `GET /agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream`.
